title: l3lint results
description: The JSON output of l3lint lint. Findings are advisory: they say a payload is likely to downgrade or meets the documented requirement. Card networks and issuers decide the rate.

tool.description: The tool that wrote the results.

rulePacks.description: Rule pack ID to pack version.

asOf.description: The --as-of date when given, else null (each transaction then carries its own as-of date).

inputs.description: Every input of the run, in the order given.

path.description: The path as given (relative paths stay relative), or - for standard input.

format.description: The format the input was read as, for example stripe; unknown when it could not be read.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the input's bytes.

transactions.description: How many transactions the input held.

inputErrors.description: Inputs, or NDJSON records, that could not be read. Each one makes the exit code at least 2.

line.description: The line where reading failed, when known.

message.description: What went wrong and what to change.

candidates.description: The formats that tied when detection could not choose; pass one with --format.

transactions.description: One entry per transaction, in input order.

batchFindings.description: Findings about the run as a whole, such as GEN-DQ-007. Each points at the first transaction that carries the repeated value.

summary.description: Counts over every finding, including findings left out by --max-findings.

byRule.description: Rule ID to the number of findings it raised.

byBrand.description: Brand to finding counts. A general rule's findings count under the transaction's brand.

findingsShown.description: Findings written to the output. Present only when --max-findings left some out.

findingsOmitted.description: Findings left out by --max-findings. Present only when above 0.

notes.description: Notes about the run, such as where the settings came from.

exitCode.description: The exit code of the run: 0 clean or below --fail-on, 1 findings at or above --fail-on, 2 usage or input error, 3 rule pack, config or internal error.

tier.description: The tier rollup for one brand: the best tier the card and MCC allow and the tier the data likely reaches.

brand.description: The brand. Present in likelyTiers entries.

best.description: The best tier the card and MCC allow, or none.

likely.description: The tier the payload likely reaches.

status.description: meets: the payload meets the documented requirements of the best tier. atRisk: Visa may still reject the data after settlement. blocked: an error finding blocks the best tier. noBenefit: no enhanced-data rate exists for this card, brand or MCC.

blockingErrors.description: How many error findings blocked tiers.

index.description: 0-based position of the transaction in the run.

input.description: 0-based index of its input in inputs.

id.description: The transaction ID from the payload.

brand.description: The effective card brand: the --brand flag, else the payload, else the config file.

brands.description: Every brand evaluated: one brand normally, all four with --brand all. Absent when the brand is unknown and only general rules ran.

format.description: The adapter that read the transaction, for example stripe.

asOf.description: The date whose rules applied: --as-of, else transactionDate, else the day of the run.

likelyTier.description: The tier rollup for the transaction's brand, or null when the brand is unknown.

likelyTiers.description: One tier rollup per evaluated brand. Present when more than one brand was evaluated.

costEstimate.description: Estimated cost from the user's rate table. Present only with --rates.

notes.description: Notes such as context overrides and adapter remarks.

findings.description: The findings, sorted by canonical path, then rule ID.

patchOperation.description: One RFC 6902 JSON Patch operation in the source format's paths and units.

path.description: JSON Pointer of the target value in the source document.

from.description: JSON Pointer of the source value, for move and copy.

value.description: The value to add, replace or test.

finding.description: One rule result on one transaction.

ruleId.description: The rule ID, for example VISA-L3-004, or an engine diagnostic ID such as L3LINT-ENGINE-001.

severity.description: The effective severity after profile scoping and overrides.

impact.description: What the finding means for the interchange tier.

brand.description: The brand whose pack raised the finding. Absent for general rules.

transactionIndex.description: 0-based index of the transaction. Present in batchFindings.

canonical.description: JSON Pointer in the canonical payload, for example /lineItems/1/commodityCode.

source.description: The same place in the original format, such as a Stripe JSON Pointer or a CSV cell label; null when the format has no such field.

location.description: Line and column of the value in the input file, or null when the value is absent or the position is unknown.

message.description: What is wrong, in plain words.

expected.description: What the rule expected, when it can be stated.

actual.description: The value found, already masked for card numbers; null when the value is absent.

fix.description: How to fix it, stated as an action.

patch.description: A mechanical RFC 6902 patch for this finding, or null when there is none.

needsHuman.description: True when a person must decide the fix, for example a proposed unit mapping. Absent otherwise.

sources.description: Public pages the rule comes from.

costEstimate.description: Estimated interchange cost from the user's rate table. Always an estimate, never the actual fee.

estimates.description: One entry per evaluated brand that has categories in the rate table.

likelyTier.description: The rate table tier used for the likely outcome.

likelyCost.description: Estimated cost at the likely tier, or null when the table has no matching category.

bestTier.description: The rate table tier used for the best outcome.

bestCost.description: Estimated cost at the best tier, or null when the table has no matching category.

difference.description: Likely cost minus best cost, when both exist: what the downgrade likely costs.
